audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central instruction is backwards, in four places. spikes[1] says Riftwalk lets you 'blink out of her tentacle field and over the spirit-pull'; wants.you[0] says 'Blink Test of Spirit and the tentacle field with Riftwalk'; mid says 'you can finally blink out of the tentacle field and over the spirit-pull'; and early says "you have to physically run from your own torn-off spirit". Running from the spirit is the one thing that must not happen.
audit.why: Riot's Test of Spirit text: 'If killed, OR IF THE TARGET GETS TOO FAR FROM THE SPIRIT, the target will become a Vessel and begin spawning Tentacles.' Blinking away from your own spirit does not escape the ability - it completes it, and turns you into a tentacle farm for the rest of the fight. This page teaches the reader to use their newly unlocked ultimate to trigger the enemy's win condition. The correct read is the reverse: once the spirit is out you stay inside its leash and get the SPIRIT away from her tentacles, because tentacles swing at spirits and the spirit echoes a percentage of the damage it takes back onto you. Riftwalk is the right button before Test of Spirit lands and the wrong one after.
audit.corrected: All four strings rewritten: blink to dodge the cast, never to leave the leash once it has landed. The Vessel condition stated explicitly.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json (E Test of Spirit: 'Spirits echo a percentage of the damage they take to the original target. If killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit, the target will become a Vessel'; P: 'Tentacles swing at spirits, Vessels, and victims of Illaoi's Harsh lesson')

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit is named the matchup-defining cooldown seven times without a number, and Harsh Lesson - her actual damage and gap-close - is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is 16/15/14/13/12s at 900 range. Harsh Lesson is a FOUR-second leap that resets her auto-attack and makes every nearby tentacle swing at the target - that is the cooldown you are actually trading against between casts of her E, and at 4s you cannot wait it out, you can only stand where the tentacles are not. Leap of Faith is 120/95/70s. Tentacle Smash is 10/9/8/7/6s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: Test of Spirit's 16s written in, Harsh Lesson named with its 4s reset, Leap of Faith's 120s added to the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Illaoi six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while spikes[3] opens 'Your window', whys[6] says 'The monster wakes', and late opens 'This is the window the whole game was about'.
audit.why: Kassadin loses this 46.15% over 13 games, so an Illaoi-heavy chart is the right shape overall. But 2+ items is the one stage where all three prose sources say the lane has changed hands, and the chart disagrees with every one of them.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Kassadin in both layers. Earlier stages left with Illaoi.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, despite the page saying 'she out-sustains you' three separate times.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God heals Illaoi whenever her tentacles damage a champion, and with Harsh Lesson on a 4-second cooldown making every nearby tentacle swing, that heal fires constantly in any extended trade. Naming Grievous Wounds turns three repetitions of an observation into an item slot.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in the all-in block against the tentacle heal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json (P: 'will heal Illaoi if they damage a champion')

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications and a pronoun. whys[2] says 'Force Pulse only refunds cooldown off nearby casts' - it charges from nearby casts, it does not refund cooldown. breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. And tldr, winCon and report[9] all call Illaoi 'him' and 'his'.
audit.why: Force Pulse must accumulate charge from spells cast in Kassadin's vicinity before it is usable at all, then sits on a flat 21/20/19/18/17s. 'Refunds cooldown' implies the ability is available and merely comes back faster, which is the opposite of the problem in a passive lane. Null Sphere's real text is damage, channel interrupt, and a magic-absorbing shield.
audit.corrected: Charge mechanic stated correctly, silence removed, pronouns fixed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (E: 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up...')

edits.before: Pre-6 this is one of your worst lanes — you have no escape, little damage, and every tentacle she plants near you turns a trade into a beating. Last-hit from the very tip of Null Sphere, keep the Q shield to eat the burst when she throws Test of Spirit, and never walk into her tentacle field to contest a wave. If she lands the spirit-pull, you have to physically run from your own torn-off spirit or her tentacles slap you for half your bar — so treat that range like a death zone and concede the CS you can't safely take. Lean on Nether Blade to keep mana up, because once your pool is empty you have nothing but autos.
edits.after: Pre-6 this is one of your worst lanes - you have no escape, little damage, and every tentacle she plants near you turns a trade into a beating. Last-hit from the very tip of Null Sphere, keep the Q shield to eat the burst when she throws Test of Spirit, and never walk into her tentacle field to contest a wave. If the spirit-pull lands, do NOT run: leaving its leash turns you into a Vessel that spawns tentacles for the rest of the fight. Stay inside the leash and walk the spirit clear of her tentacles instead, since it echoes back a share of everything they hit it with. Lean on Nether Blade to keep mana up.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are pure survival: Null Sphere the wave from range, restore mana off Nether Blade, and track Test of Spirit only so it doesn't kill you on the way to 6. Riftwalk is your release valve — once it's up you can finally blink out of the tentacle field and over the spirit-pull, the first time all game you get to dictate distance. Don't get greedy with it yet; she still out-sustains and out-trades you on her field, so blink to dodge and farm, not to duel. Rod of Ages / Catalyst stalls you toward even, and your only job here is to not die until your AP items come online.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are pure survival: Null Sphere the wave from range, restore mana off Nether Blade, and track Test of Spirit's 16s only so it doesn't kill you on the way to 6. Riftwalk is your release valve, but it dodges the cast, not the consequence - blink as she winds up, never after the spirit is out, because leaving the leash makes you a Vessel. Her real trading tool is Harsh Lesson: a 4-second leap that resets her auto and makes every nearby tentacle swing, so stand where the tentacles are not. Rod of Ages stalls you toward even; your job is to not die.

edits.before: This is the window the whole game was about. At 2+ items your stacked Riftwalk recasts, ability haste, and AP let you blink repeatedly — and Illaoi is exactly the immobile, field-bound bruiser your kit was built to dodge and outlast. Never stand in her tentacle field to fight; blink in on a tentacle's wind-down, chunk her with Q into Riftwalk, and blink out before the next slap lands. In teamfights she has to commit Leap of Faith to one spot, so let her plant her tentacle ring and flank from the side she didn't — then blink onto their backline carries while she's stuck swinging at empty ground. You're the slipperiest threat in the lobby and she simply can't catch you off her field.
edits.after: This is the window the whole game was about. At 2+ items your Riftwalk sits at 2s and your AP has arrived - and Illaoi is exactly the immobile, field-bound bruiser your kit was built to dodge and outlast. Never stand in her tentacle field to fight; blink in on a tentacle's wind-down, chunk her with Q into Riftwalk, and blink out before Harsh Lesson resets four seconds later. Buy Grievous Wounds first, because every tentacle that connects heals her. In teamfights she has to commit Leap of Faith to one spot, so let her plant her tentacle ring and flank from the side she didn't - then blink onto their backline while she swings at empty ground. She simply can't catch you off her field.

notes: THE PAGE TAUGHT THE OPPOSITE OF THE CORRECT PLAY, in four places. spikes[1], wants.you[0], mid and early all told the reader to use Riftwalk to blink away from Test of Spirit's spirit, or to 'physically run from your own torn-off spirit'. Riot's own text: 'If killed, OR IF THE TARGET GETS TOO FAR FROM THE SPIRIT, the target will become a Vessel and begin spawning Tentacles.' Blinking out of the leash does not escape the ability, it completes it - the page was instructing a Kassadin player to spend their level-6 spike triggering Illaoi's win condition. Rewritten so Riftwalk dodges the CAST and the reader stays inside the leash afterwards, walking the spirit clear of tentacles because the spirit echoes a share of the damage it takes. Also corrected: whys[2] said 'Force Pulse only refunds cooldown off nearby casts' - it must CHARGE from nearby casts before it is usable, then sits on a flat 21/20/19/18/17s; breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence (it has none); and tldr, winCon and report[9] all referred to Illaoi as 'him'/'his'. Added: Harsh Lesson, her 4-second auto-resetting leap that makes nearby tentacles swing, was never named anywhere despite being the cooldown you actually trade against, and Grievous Wounds against the tentacle heal that three separate strings complain about. FLAG FOR REVIEW: the derived kit flags list 'grounding' and 'untargetable' on Leap of Faith. Riot's own description of Leap of Faith mentions neither, and grounding would matter enormously here because it would deny Riftwalk. I have written nothing either way - see unverified.
